div.div:
Retired, kept for the record: F6 load score / F7 recommendation.
The plan was inside the score: shift steps 5.77 points apart, the model's say inside a step 0.106 — 54× smaller. A score that contains the plan cannot test the plan against demand.

div.div:
Resident
“Why was my street cleared later than the next one?”
→ Your zone was planned for shift N of 5 — the order was published in advance.
→ Here is how many reports your zone filed, next to what similar storms would lead one to expect, with the uncertainty shown.

div.div:
City operations / reviewer
“Did last storm's plan line up with where demand was?”
→ Prompts point at zones where heavy demand met a late shift, and say how stable that is.
→ Routes, equipment and road network are not in the data — the decision stays the city's.

div.div:
WHO GETS PLOWED FIRST?
The published plan already answers it.
H2 adds the part that can be checked: did demand agree with the order, and how sure can we be? — so a review can start from evidence rather than from who complained loudest.

div.div: What the page never says: “the plan was wrong” · “a late shift is unfair” · “forecast” for a backtest · “plan last updated …” (the schedule has no update field) · “the model beats the baseline” (not defensible on 7 holdout storms)
